text.p: Following are the main stories in Thursday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The youth and women wings of Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) voted in Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Siti Zaharah Sulaiman as new leaders in their respective elections, with both scoring upset victories over the incumbents.
-- Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said corruption could never be eradicated as long as party members retain their shameless behaviour of trading their dignity for a small profit.

-- Siti Zaharah scored a major upset when she deposed incumbent and International Trade and Industry Minister Rafidah Aziz for the post of UMNO women's wing chief by a 27-vote margin at the party elections.
-- Eleven pupils of a primary school in Sarawak state were burnt to death in a fire which destroyed their wooden hostel.
-- Shell Malaysia has embarked on a 615 million ringgit project to create its very first unmanned remote-control production platform for its operations in Malaysia.
